title_en: Wang Gengdi, Quan Xueli, Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei — case of theft and speculation
keywords_en: Criminal; Theft; Speculation; Second Instance; High People's Court; Shaanxi Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Determination of Principal and Accessory; Characterization of Theft vs. Speculation; Determination of Recidivism; Appropriateness of Sentencing; Affirmation of Original Judgment; Theft of Cultural Relics; Trafficking of Cultural Relics; Terracotta Warrior Head; Embezzlement
full_text_en:
Wang Gengdi, Quan Xueli, Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei — theft and speculation case

Defendant Wang Gengdi, male, 21 years old, farmer from Wanli Village, Kangqiao Township, Lintong County, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant Quan Xueli, male, 23 years old, formerly a passenger attendant at Lintong Railway Station, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant Tang Ke, male, 43 years old, formerly a temporary worker at the Meilihua Hotel, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province. In 1982, he was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of embezzlement.

Defendant Zhang Chuanxiu, male, 33 years old, formerly a worker at Lintong County Third Transportation Company, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant Sun Zhenping, male, 29 years old, formerly manager of Beixin Hostel, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

All of the above defendants were arrested on July 3, 1987.

Defendant Fan Chunmei, female, 46 years old, from Zhashui County, Shaanxi Province, unemployed. She was arrested on September 22, 1987.

In the case of defendants Wang Gengdi, Quan Xueli, Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei for theft and speculation, the Xi'an Municipal People's Procuratorate, Shaanxi Province, initiated a public prosecution with the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court. After accepting the case and conducting a public trial, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court found:

One day in January 1987, while defendants Wang Gengdi and Quan Xueli were dining at a canteen near Lintong Railway Station, Quan Xueli said that trading in cultural relics was the most profitable business and asked Wang Gengdi to steal a terracotta warrior head, promising to find a buyer for it. A few days later, Quan Xueli urged Wang Gengdi for the terracotta warrior head. At that point, Wang Gengdi decided to commit the theft. At around midnight on February 17, 1987, Wang Gengdi, carrying a screwdriver, climbed over the wall into the Qinling Museum compound, then entered the Qinling Archaeological Team office, pried open the door, and stole one Qin-dynasty high-ranking military officer's terracotta head (commonly known as a general's terracotta head, a Grade One, Category A national precious cultural relic). He hid it in a grove north of the Lintong Railway Station tracks. On the night of February 18, Wang Gengdi showed Quan Xueli the stolen high-ranking military officer's terracotta head. Quan Xueli promised to find a buyer immediately. That same night, Wang Gengdi moved the general's terracotta head to an empty room in a warehouse at Lintong 03; a few days later, he moved it again to the dormitory of defendant Zhang Chuanxiu for concealment. During this period, when Quan Xueli asked his elder brother to help find a buyer, he was criticized and refused, so the fencing failed. Thereafter, Quan Xueli no longer participated in the criminal activities of selling the general's terracotta head. Around mid-April, Zhang Chuanxiu brought defendant Tang Ke to his dormitory to see the general's terracotta head. To distinguish the genuine article from fakes, Zhang Chuanxiu and Tang Ke went together to the Qinling Museum and a cultural relic replica market to observe and compare the general's terracotta head. On April 29, Wang Gengdi and Zhang Chuanxiu brought the general's terracotta head to Tang Ke's home. The three agreed that after the sale, aside from giving Wang Gengdi RMB 50,000, the surplus proceeds would be split equally between Tang Ke and Zhang Chuanxiu. One evening in early May, defendant Sun Zhenping, upon seeing the general's terracotta head at Tang Ke's home, expressed willingness to find a buyer for it. In early June, Sun Zhenping said to defendant Fan Chunmei: "A friend of mine has a general's terracotta head for sale. Find a buyer for it." Fan Chunmei agreed immediately. On June 16, when Tang Ke, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei were negotiating the price at the Beixin Hostel, they all felt that the selling price of RMB 250,000 was too low and demanded a higher price. On June 17, while Tang Ke, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei were attempting to sell the general's terracotta head for RMB 300,000 at the Beixin Hostel, they were caught on the spot by public security authorities.

The facts of the crimes of the above-listed defendants Wang Gengdi, Quan Xueli, Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and each defendant has confessed.

After trial, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court held that defendants Wang Gengdi, Quan Xueli, and defendants Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei jointly committed crimes, constituting joint intentional crimes as defined in Article 22, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. In the joint intentional crime, Wang Gengdi actively carried tools, pried open the door, entered the premises alone, stole the Grade One, Category A national precious cultural relic—the Qin high-ranking military officer's terracotta head—and actively contacted buyers for fencing; Quan Xueli asked Wang Gengdi to steal the national precious cultural relic, suggested the theft target to Wang Gengdi, and afterward actively sought buyers; Tang Ke and Zhang Chuanxiu, knowing that the Qin general's terracotta head was a national precious cultural relic, actively sought buyers to engage in speculation for exorbitant profits. Pursuant to Article 23, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, they are all principal offenders in this case. Sun Zhenping and Fan Chunmei, knowing that the law strictly prohibited the sale of cultural relics, actively participated in the speculative activities of selling the general's terracotta head for exorbitant profits. Pursuant to Article 24, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Law, they are accomplices in this case and shall be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offenders. Wang Gengdi and Quan Xueli jointly stole a national precious cultural relic, and their acts constitute the crime of theft as defined in Article 152 of the Criminal Law. Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, Sun Zhenping, and Fan Chunmei engaged in illegal speculative activities in cultural relics, seeking exorbitant profits, and have thereby constituted the crime of speculation as defined in Article 118 of the Criminal Law. Tang Ke was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for embezzlement in 1982; within three years after his release from prison, he again committed an offense punishable by imprisonment or heavier punishment, and pursuant to Article 61, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, he is a recidivist and shall be given a heavier punishment. However, after the criminal facts of this case were exposed, Tang Ke had a relatively good attitude in admitting his guilt and was able to assist the public security authorities in apprehending criminals, so a discretionary lighter punishment may be applied. The acts of Tang Ke, Zhang Chuanxiu, and Sun Zhenping seriously disrupted social order, and pursuant to Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. Wang Gengdi's theft of a national precious cultural relic was of an extremely odious nature and particularly serious circumstances; in accordance with Item (1) of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, he shall be severely punished. Accordingly, on October 7, 1987, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court sentenced defendant Wang Gengdi to death for the crime of theft, sentenced Quan Xueli to life imprisonment for the crime of theft, and, pursuant to Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, deprived Wang Gengdi and Quan Xueli of their political rights for life. For the crime of speculation, it sentenced defendant Tang Ke to fifteen years' imprisonment with deprivation of political rights for three years; Zhang Chuanxiu to thirteen years' imprisonment with deprivation of political rights for two years; Sun Zhenping to ten years' imprisonment with deprivation of political rights for two years; and Fan Chunmei to eight years' imprisonment.

After the first-instance judgment, Wang Gengdi appealed on the ground that he stole the cultural relic under duress from others and was not the principal offender; Quan Xueli appealed on the ground that he did not instruct Wang Gengdi to steal the cultural relic and the sentence was too heavy; Zhang Chuanxiu appealed on the ground that some individual facts in the original judgment were untrue and that he had no purpose of seeking profit; Tang Ke and Sun Zhenping appealed on the grounds that they only played a connecting role in the sale of the general's terracotta head, that the original judgment's conviction was incorrect, and that the sentence was too heavy; Fan Chunmei appealed on the ground that when contacting the buyer, she did not know it was a general's terracotta head and did not participate in the speculation, and therefore should not be convicted of the crime of speculation. They each appealed to the Shaanxi High People's Court.

After trial, the Shaanxi High People's Court held: Appellant Wang Gengdi carried tools, entered the premises alone by prying open the door, stole a national precious cultural relic, and actively contacted buyers for fencing; he was clearly the principal offender in this case. His appeal ground was purely an attempt to shift responsibility and could not be sustained. Appellant Quan Xueli actively conspired with Wang Gengdi to steal a national precious cultural relic, suggested the theft target to Wang Gengdi, and afterward sought buyers for him, playing an important role in the theft activities; his appeal ground likewise could not be sustained. Appellant Zhang Chuanxiu actively contacted buyers to engage in speculation for exorbitant profits; the criminal facts are not only confirmed by the confessions of Wang Gengdi and Tang Ke but also by Zhang Chuanxiu's own multiple confessions on record, which is sufficient to establish the case; his appeal ground could not be sustained. Appellant Tang Ke, knowing that the general's terracotta head was a national precious cultural relic, colluded with other offenders to actively engage in speculative activities; he was clearly a principal offender in the crime of speculation; his appeal ground could not be sustained. Appellant Sun Zhenping, as manager of the Beixin Hostel, actively participated in the criminal activities of selling the general's terracotta head for exorbitant profits and provided the premises for the crime; his appeal ground could not be sustained. Appellant Fan Chunmei, knowing it was the general's terracotta head, participated in the criminal activities of selling cultural relics for exorbitant profits; this is confirmed by witness testimony and the confessions of co-defendants Sun Zhenping and Tang Ke; her appeal ground could not be sustained. The original judgment had clear findings of fact, reliable and sufficient evidence, appropriate sentencing, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures. Accordingly, after discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee of this court on October 15, 1987, in accordance with Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled that the appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

In accordance with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court authorizing the High People's Courts to approve certain death penalty cases, the Shaanxi High People's Court approved the judgment of the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court sentencing Wang Gengdi to death and deprivation of political rights for life for the crime of theft.
